title: Conditional Memory via Scalable Lookup: A New Axis of Sparsity for Large Language Models

follow_ups_checked.paper: Frozen Memory Is Not Enough arXiv:2608.17050v3

reading_coverage.method: downloaded official PDFs from arXiv; extracted full text with PyMuPDF; read sections listed

claims.claim: Transformers lack native lookup; entity resolution consumes multiple early layers (Diana example)
surjective canonical ID mapping (NFKC, lowercase); 23% effective vocab reduction for 128k tokenizer
K hash heads per order, prime-sized tables, multiplicative-XOR hash; concat to e_t ∈ R^{d_mem}
alpha_t = sigmoid(RMSNorm(h)·RMSNorm(W_K e)/sqrt(d)); depthwise causal conv kernel 4, dilation = max order, SiLU; H ← H + Y
shared table and W_V, M distinct W_K across mHC branches (M=4); fused FP8 matmul
training: sharded tables with All-to-All; inference: prefetch from host memory; Zipf multi-level cache proposed
U-shape over rho at 2e20 and 6e20 FLOPs; optimum rho≈75–80%; 6e20: 1.7248→1.7109; rho≈40% matches pure MoE
3B backbone, slots 2.58e5→1e7 (up to ~13B params), log-linear loss; better than OverEncoding

Engram-27B vs MoE-27B (262B tokens, 3.8B act): MMLU 57.4→60.4, BBH 50.9→55.9, CMMLU 57.9→61.9, ARC-C 70.1→73.8, HumanEval 37.8→40.8, MATH 28.3→30.7, CCPM 79.6→87.1, PopQA 19.2→19.4; 72→55 routed experts, 5.7B memory, rho=74.3%
abstract and §1 state MMLU +3.4; Table 1 and §4.2 give +3.0 (57.4→60.4); reading uses +3.0
claims.locator: Abstract p1, §1 p2, Table 1 p9, §4.2 p11

claims.claim: Engram-40B (18.5B memory) improves most benchmarks; HumanEval 38.4, MBPP 46.2, C3 61.8, MATH 30.6 below Engram-27B; attributed to under-training
32k YaRN extension 5000 steps/30B tokens; MQ-NIAH 84.2→97.0, VT 77.0→87.2 (iso-loss 46k); S-NIAH 100.0 vs 97.6
LogitLens lower KL in early layers; CKA: Engram layer 5 ≈ MoE layer 12
3B MoE baseline 1.808; single module best at layer 2 (1.770); layers 2+6 1.768; key components: multi-branch, gating, tokenizer compression; conv minor; 4-gram slightly worse
disable Engram at inference: factual 29–44% retained (TriviaQA 29%), reading comprehension 81–93%; MATH 36%, MGSM 44%, GSM8K 62%
Engram-27B: layers [2,15], N-gram [2,3], 8 heads, d_mem 1280, Engram vocab 2,262,400 (40B: 7,239,680), Adam lr ×5, no weight decay, conv zero init, Muon backbone
V4 does not include Engram; first 3 MoE layers use hash routing by token ID; future work cites more sparse embedding modules (Cheng et al., 2026)

V4.1-Flash: 196B Engram in two modules at layers 1 and 14 (zero-indexed), orders {2,3,4}, 8 heads, 2048 dim per order, ~16M entries per head, FP8; conv removed; momentum + Sinkhorn balancing instead of Adam; tables stay in GPU during RL rollouts; lr ×5

XOR hash couples table to tokenizer; polynomial byte hashing with joint space + 1-gram; mean 0.605 (XOR) vs 0.612 (poly); cross-tokenizer frozen transfer 0.560→0.584; N=1 control no gain; bits/byte with Engram 0.919 vs base 0.861
